citation: Schoen, R. C., LaVenia, M., Tazaz, A., Farina, K., Dixon, J. K., & Secada, W. G. (2020). Replicating the CGI Experiment in Diverse Environments: Effects on Grade 1 and 2 Student Mathematics Achievement in the First Program Year (Research Report No. 2020-02). Tallahassee, FL: Florida Center for Research in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (FCR-STEM), Learning Systems Institute, Florida State University. https://doi.org/10.33009/fsu.1601237075
report_number: FSU Research Report No. 2020-02 (IES Award R305A120781); FSU DigiNole object fsu:758407
design: Multisite cluster-randomized controlled trial (RCT); assignment level = School. 22 elementary schools in two adjacent Florida public school districts (District A = large urban, 15 schools; District B = 7 schools), randomized within FRL-stratified randomization blocks: 11 treatment vs 11 comparison schools. Intervention = Cognitively Guided Instruction (CGI) mathematics teacher professional-development program (Year 1 of a 3-year model delivered by Teachers Development Group, TDG) for grade-1 and grade-2 teachers. Comparison = schools invited to participate in a different district-chosen PD program that did NOT focus on number, operations, or algebraic thinking (treated by the meta-analysis as the business-as-usual/no-math-PD contrast). Subject = mathematics; grades 1-2 (registry grade band K-2). End-of-Year-1 (spring 2014) student achievement on three outcomes: MPAC interview (researcher/developer-made), ITBS Math Problems and ITBS Math Computation (standardized). Impacts estimated via 3-level Bayesian multilevel regression (students in classrooms in schools), pretest- and covariate-adjusted. Confirmatory analytic samples: ITBS N=2,172 (T=1,123; C=1,049) early+late joiners; MPAC N=622 (T=305; C=317) early joiners only.
problems: 1) The DOI/FSU repository download URL is behind an AWS WAF JavaScript challenge that blocks direct curl GET (HTTP 202 'x-amzn-waf-action: challenge', returns 0-byte body); the valid 140-page, 2.5 MB PDF was obtained from the Wayback Machine raw snapshot (https://web.archive.org/web/20250612154602id_/https://repository.lib.fsu.edu/islandora/object/fsu:758407/datastream/PDF/download) and saved to data/fulltext/schoen_2020.pdf (the 'url' field records the canonical source URL). 2) COMPARISON CONDITION CAVEAT: comparison schools were not strictly do-nothing; they were invited to a different district-chosen PD program that did not target math number/operations/algebraic thinking. The meta-analysis coded this as the (no-math-PD) business-as-usual contrast (registry: targeted_population 'All', tpd_goal '(P)CK'). 3) The report standardizes effect sizes per WWC guidance as g = J * (regression coefficient / unadjusted pooled within-group SD based on total variance), so I used the report's directly reported Hedges' g values (Tables 5.1, 5.2). The Table 5.2 'Estimate' column is on a (near-)standardized outcome metric (outcome variances ~1; recovered standardizing SD ~1.0-1.13), so the posterior SD (PSD) is effectively the standard error of g; I report impact_estimate = the Model-3 treatment coefficient and impact_se = its PSD, and computed g_se = |g| * (PSD/|b|) (= J*PSD/SD), g_var = g_se^2. These are Bayesian credibility-interval-based; none of the three confirmatory main effects reached conventional significance (all 95% CIs include zero). 4) ICC: I recorded the unconditional (Model 0) between-school ICC as the design-effect ICC for each outcome (MPAC .062, ITBS-MP .027, ITBS-MC .029) from Appendix D Tables D.1-D.3; cluster_adjusted=true because g and its SE come from the 3-level multilevel model. 5) n_t/n_c are student-level analytic Ns (Table 2.3); n_clusters=22 schools. 6) Grade-1 and grade-2 splits (Table 5.3) are subgroups (is_full_sample=false) and are recorded in notes only, not as separate full-sample rows.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CGI teacher PD (Year 1) vs comparison schools (different non-math-focused district PD / business-as-usual)
effect_sizes.test_name: Iowa Test of Basic Skills - Math Problems (ITBS-MP), cross-grade vertically scaled score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / spring 2014 (end of first program year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's directly reported Hedges' g (Table 5.1 / Table 5.2, Model 3 confirmatory, aggregate early+late-joiner sample), computed by the authors per WWC as g = J * (multilevel-model treatment coefficient / unadjusted pooled within-group SD using total variance). Model-3 standardized treatment coefficient b = 0.034 (PSD = 0.104). g_se = |g| * (PSD/|b|) = 0.03 * (0.104/0.034) = 0.0918 (equivalently J*PSD/SD); g_var = g_se^2 = 0.00842. J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = 2170 (J~0.99965). mean/SD are unadjusted posttest descriptives (Table A.5); the impact is the covariate-/pretest-adjusted model coefficient.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5.1 & Table 5.2 (pp. 39-40, PDF pp. 54-55); Appendix D Table D.2 (PDF pp. 89-90); descriptives Table A.5 (p. 69, PDF p. 54); Ns Table 2.3 (p. 11)
effect_sizes.notes: RQ1 confirmatory outcome. ITBS Math Problems: word-problem / applications-of-mathematics measure. Model 3 (full covariate + baseline-adjusted): g = 0.03, gamma=0.034, 95% CI [-0.171, 0.244], not significant. Unadjusted/less-adjusted models: Model 1 g=0.10, Model 2 g=0.05. Sensitivity analyses: early-joiners only g=0.03; maximum-likelihood g=0.02. Grade subgroups (Table 5.3, is_full_sample=false, NOT extracted as rows): grade 1 g=0.14 (N=1,103), grade 2 g=-0.07 (N=1,069).

effect_sizes.arm_label: CGI teacher PD (Year 1) vs comparison schools (different non-math-focused district PD / business-as-usual)
effect_sizes.test_name: Iowa Test of Basic Skills - Math Computation (ITBS-MC), cross-grade vertically scaled score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / spring 2014 (end of first program year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's directly reported Hedges' g (Table 5.1 / Table 5.2, Model 3 confirmatory, aggregate early+late-joiner sample), WWC method (g = J * model treatment coefficient / unadjusted pooled within-group SD). Model-3 standardized treatment coefficient b = -0.110 (PSD = 0.113). g_se = |g| * (PSD/|b|) = 0.11 * (0.113/0.110) = 0.1130 (= J*PSD/SD); g_var = g_se^2 = 0.01277. df = 2170, J~0.99965. mean/SD are unadjusted posttest descriptives (Table A.5).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5.1 & Table 5.2 (pp. 39-40, PDF pp. 54-55); Appendix D Table D.3 (PDF pp. 91-92); descriptives Table A.5 (p. 69, PDF p. 54); Ns Table 2.3 (p. 11)
effect_sizes.notes: RQ1 confirmatory outcome. ITBS Math Computation: addition/subtraction computational ability. Model 3: g = -0.11 (NEGATIVE, favoring comparison), gamma=-0.110, 95% CI [-0.338, 0.114], not significant in confirmatory Bayesian analysis. Models 1/2: g=-0.07, -0.11. The likelihood-based sensitivity analysis reached conventional significance (gamma=-0.11, p=.02). Authors attribute the negative effect to the Year-1 content focusing on grade-1 mathematics while grade-2 computational expectations are higher. Grade subgroups (Table 5.3, is_full_sample=false, NOT extracted): grade 1 g=0.03 (N=1,103), grade 2 g=-0.29 (N=1,069).

effect_sizes.arm_label: CGI teacher PD (Year 1) vs comparison schools (different non-math-focused district PD / business-as-usual)
effect_sizes.test_name: Mathematics Performance and Cognition (MPAC) interview, vertically scaled score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post / spring 2014 (end of first program year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's directly reported Hedges' g (Table 5.1 / Table 5.2, Model 3 confirmatory, MPAC analytic sample = early joiners only since MPAC was administered only to early joiners), WWC method (g = J * model treatment coefficient / unadjusted pooled within-group SD). Model-3 standardized treatment coefficient b = 0.083 (PSD = 0.168). g_se = |g| * (PSD/|b|) = 0.08 * (0.168/0.083) = 0.1619 (= J*PSD/SD); g_var = g_se^2 = 0.02622. df = 620, J~0.99879. mean/SD are unadjusted posttest descriptives (Table A.5); MPAC posttest is reported on a z-scaled metric.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5.1 & Table 5.2 (pp. 39-40, PDF pp. 54-55); Appendix D Table D.1 (PDF pp. 87-88); descriptives Table A.5 (p. 69, PDF p. 54); Ns Table 2.3 (p. 11)
effect_sizes.notes: RQ1 confirmatory outcome. MPAC = one-on-one researcher/developer-made mathematics interview (number, operations, equality; problem solving and algebraic thinking). Researcher-made, so likely excluded by the meta-analysis's independent-measure filter, but extracted and labeled per spec. Model 3: g = 0.08, gamma=0.083, 95% CI [-0.253, 0.417], not significant. Less-adjusted: Model 1 g=0.20, Model 2 g=0.14. Sensitivity: maximum-likelihood g=0.10. Grade subgroups (Table 5.3, is_full_sample=false, NOT extracted): grade 1 g=0.25 (N=336), grade 2 g=-0.01 (N=286).
